## The dataset, and what makes our variant special

DrivAerML is 484 parametrically morphed DrivAer notchback variants with
time-averaged fields from scale-resolving CFD — surface pressure and
wall shear on ~8.8M-point vehicle surfaces, plus volume fields. It is
"steady" in the statistically-stationary sense of the RANS charter:
the labels are time averages of a turbulent flow, which is exactly the
setting the program's scope was written for (the closure is empirical;
the equations are not given).

The variant used here (the internal BC-labeled curation) differs from
the public distribution in the one way this program cares about most:
**every case carries the actual boundary-value problem.** Five named,
BC-typed boundary meshes — the `vehicle`, a `no_slip` ground plane
beginning just ahead of the car, `slip` tunnel walls and ceiling, an
`inlet`, and an `outlet` — plus per-case freestream values
($U_\infty$, $p_\infty$, $\rho_\infty$, $\nu$, $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$) as
global data. The public release ships only the vehicle geometry, which
is the interesting *shape* but not the posed *problem*.

## The standing hypothesis

Every model currently wired into the unified external-aero recipe
consumes only the vehicle surface; the other four labeled boundaries
sit in the data unused. The `MeshTransformer`'s typed-boundary schema
consumes all five natively — and the mixed-BC discriminator suite
(@sec-mixed-bc) measured exactly this setting as the place attention
earns its keep.

- **H-ground (the headline experiment).** Feeding all five typed
  boundaries beats the vehicle-only formulation on surface pressure
  near the underbody and wake, because ground effect is real physics
  that the vehicle-only formulation must hallucinate from shape priors.
  *Falsifier: five-boundary arm no better than vehicle-only at matched
  budget and matched sampling — which would mean the fixed far
  boundaries are adequately encoded in the freestream vector alone,
  itself a publishable negative.*

## Integration plan

The recipe is `DomainMesh`-native and registry-free: a new model is one
YAML under `conf/model/` declaring `forward_kwargs` resolved from
DomainMesh paths. The `MeshTransformer` enters as a mesh-native model
(the same pattern the in-tree GLOBE configs use), with two arms:

1. `mesh_transformer_vehicle` — `boundaries.vehicle` only, matching
   every existing model's information diet (the fair-comparison arm);
2. `mesh_transformer_allbc` — all five typed boundaries (the
   H-ground arm).

Surface task first (pressure + wall shear at surface centroids;
force-coefficient integration comes free from the recipe's inference
path), volume task second. Training at the recipe's sampling
resolution (50k–200k surface points, batch 1) requires the
checkpointed decode — the wall and its fix are @sec-scale's story,
whose paired B200 measurement accompanies this campaign.

## Results {#sec-drivaerml-results}

Two campaigns resolved here. The first answered the chapter's
pre-registered question (H-ground) — with its falsifier, in the
neutral form. The second was not planned in this chapter at all: a
40× deficit against the recipe's incumbent triggered a
root-cause investigation (@sec-nb-geot-gap) whose constructive
output — the boundary-trace mode plus two protocol findings, and the
capacity rungs they unlocked — ultimately moved the program's
DrivAerML floor by 14.5× with a per-step mechanism attribution (the
ledger below).

### H-ground: level, and honestly answered

Three arms at matched 500-epoch, 4-node protocol (1 seed/arm;
provenance `output/drivaer_v2/*.log`, HSG): vehicle-only val
**0.1019**, all-five-boundaries **0.1026**, per-boundary-pooled
**0.1036**. The pre-registered falsifier fires in its neutral form
(@sec-nb-hground-verdict): with the vehicle-starvation and
drive-overflow confounds fixed, the four labeled tunnel boundaries
neither help nor hurt. At 722 panels for an entire ground plane, the
far boundaries carry little exploitable signal beyond what the
freestream vector already encodes — **for surface-field prediction at
this resolution, the boundary-value problem's far boundaries are
adequately encoded in the freestream.** A publishable negative, per
the pre-registration; caveats attached: single seed per arm, no
banded underbody/wake decomposition.

Two pipeline findings from this campaign outlived it (both
upstreamed): the reader's dual-cap subsampling starved the vehicle to
378 cells (fixed by the topology-aware reader, PR #1819), and the
norm-free drive stream overflows on raw dimensional freestreams
(fixed by unit-direction encoding — a model *lesson*, not a bug: the
zero-preserving stream is deliberately norm-free, so its inputs must
arrive nondimensionalized).

### The gap investigation and the trace mechanism

Every capacity variant at the v2 protocol crowded into one band —
plain 0.1019, members 0.0999, wide 0.0990, allbc/pooled 0.102–0.104 —
while GeoTransolver reached 0.061 after *one epoch* under the
identical trainer. The investigation (@sec-nb-geot-gap-verdict)
killed the metric and data hypotheses and isolated two mechanisms:
a representational floor specific to on-boundary queries (H-D), and
a representational-efficiency gap (H-C).

H-D's constructive fix is the **boundary-trace mode**: surface
queries sit exactly on the double layer's jump discontinuity, and the
closed form serves the *interior* limit (−½) where the physics needs
the *exterior* trace (+½). Declaring the query mesh to be the
boundary licenses the exact one-sided correction plus own-cell typed
read-outs (@sec-nb-trace-mode). Verdict at protocol end
(@sec-nb-trace-verdict): **the pre-registered ≥5× acceptance is
REFUTED — measured 2.03×** (0.1019 → 0.0503) — but trace is the only
intervention that ever broke the 0.10 plateau, and the corrected arm
then plateaus again at ~0.049. The floor moved, and stopped: the
signature of the *next* representational ceiling, owned by H-C.
(The 2.03× is trace's effect at the small pre-ladder configuration;
the completed factorial later measured **3.8× at flagship
capacity** — mechanisms scale individually, and this one grew.
@sec-drivaerml-trace-factorial.)

### The capacity ladder, post-trace (T2)

With the trace floor removed, does capacity buy accuracy again?
Matched 1-node protocol on GB300 (single seed per rung — the
pre-registered ladder design; provenance `output/drivaer_t2/*.log`,
AGA):

| rung | final val (ep500) | vs trace |
|---|---|---|
| trace (reference dims) | 0.0288 | — |
| trace + ranks 2× | 0.0284 | +1.4% (noise) |
| **trace + operator_layers 2** | **0.0228** | **+26%** |

The ladder is *selectively* ordered (@sec-nb-t2-verdict): encoder
**depth** buys a solid 26%; attention **rank** buys nothing. The
post-trace floor is limited by the compositional depth of boundary
processing, not the width of the attention bottleneck. The depth
rung's single-seed caveat is resolved: 3-seed finals
0.0228/0.0224/0.0212 (@sec-nb-probes-verdict) — tight spread, the
+26% holds.

### The effective-batch windfall

The ladder's cross-cluster control produced its own finding: the
*identical* trace configuration reads **0.0288 at 1-node** (108
optimizer steps/epoch) vs **0.0503 at the 16-GPU protocol** (27
steps/epoch) — 1.75× better from effective batch size alone, at a
500-epoch budget. Consequence, flagged wherever numbers cross
protocols: **no cross-protocol comparison in this chapter is valid
without a matched-batch control**, including against the
GeoTransolver anchor — hence the matched 1-node control in the next
section.

The windfall's converse later closed the multi-node question
(@sec-nb-mn-verdict): 4-node DDP at matched LR and the same
500-epoch budget pays **1.58× (flagship), 1.56× (×2), ~2.2× (×4)**
against its 1-node twin — the effective-batch penalty does not
shrink with model scale. Multi-node buys wall-clock for inference
and production retrains; ladder rungs stay 1-node.

The mechanism itself was then isolated by the pre-registered 2×2
(@sec-nb-b22-verdict): a 16-GPU arm run for 2000 epochs — matching
the 1-node arm's optimizer-update count — finals at 0.0212
(2 seeds), against 0.0221 for the 500-epoch 16-GPU arm and 0.0140
for 1-node. Quadrupling the updates at large batch recovers only
~11% of the small-batch advantage: **the effective-batch effect is
the gradient noise (small-batch regularization) itself, not
optimizer-step count.** Held equal within the 16-GPU column:
configuration, learning rate, schedule shape, and data; the
1-node column's schedule differs by its queries-per-step scaling,
by design of the original comparison — the clean isolation is the
16-GPU column, and it is decisive.

### The ledger

$$
\underbrace{0.1019}_{\text{v2 protocol}}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{exterior trace (exact)}}\;
\underbrace{0.0503}_{2.03\times}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{effective batch}}\;
\underbrace{0.0288}_{1.75\times}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{encoder depth}}\;
\underbrace{0.0224}_{1.29\times}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{composition}}\;
\underbrace{0.0140}_{1.60\times}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{scale}\ (\times 2\ \text{dims})}\;
\underbrace{0.0093}_{1.51\times}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{scale}\ (\times\ \text{depth})}\;
\underbrace{0.00702}_{1.32\times}
$$

**Fourteen-and-a-half-fold, in six named steps** — jump relation,
optimization steps, compositional depth, mechanism composition, and
parameters along two confirmed axes — each a licensed, understood
mechanism, not a tuning outcome (depth is the 3-seed value; the
composition and scale steps are detailed in the sections below). The
distance to the incumbent is quoted only against the
matched-protocol control (next section).

### The matched incumbent control, and where the gap lives

The 1-node GeoTransolver control finished at **0.00249** (ep499) —
within 2% of its 16-GPU anchor, so the incumbent gains nothing from
the batch effect that gave us 1.75×. Against the ledger's endpoint:
**2.8× at the ×2L4 rung** (0.00702), down from 40× at the start
of the investigation — and the scale-law section below turns that
single ratio into a curve. Per-epoch wall-clock is comparable between the
models at this protocol; what the sections below decompose is *where*
the remaining distance lives (@sec-nb-tail-verdict,
@sec-nb-t3-launch).

The efficiency probes locate it further — and then, on the strongest
base, exclude the leading suspect. **P1** (optimizer): refuted by
inspection — both models share the trainer's exact settings. **P2**
(local-geometry diagnostic; deliberately contract-breaking, never a
keeper): CONFIRMED for efficiency *on the singpair-trace base* —
persistently ~100 epochs ahead at equal quality — but only +7% at
the converged floor. **P3** (supervision density): ¼-density costs
~35% at protocol end. That P2 signature motivated a declared local
corrector (classical BIE-style near-field structure in the decoder),
gated on a pre-registered probe ladder — and **the probes returned a
triple null** (@sec-nb-probes-verdict). On the deep2+members base,
the same local information — entering through the decode kernel (A),
restricted to a subtended-angle near field (B), or replaced by a
matched-width global latent (C) — moves neither the efficiency curve
nor the floor:

| arm (seed 43) | ep25 | ep50 | ep100 | ep~300 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| control (deep2+members) | 0.0487 | 0.0341 | 0.0234 | 0.0213 |
| A: kernel-side local | 0.0488 | 0.0352 | 0.0247 | 0.0226 |
| B: near-field only | 0.0467 | 0.0347 | 0.0244 | 0.0225 |
| C: global-latent control | 0.0461 | 0.0355 | 0.0246 | 0.0227 |

Synthesis: **local-geometry information is subsumed by
depth+members capacity** — the strong base learns whatever those
features encode quickly on its own (the same subsumption pattern as
the AirFRANS pseudo-composition result, one level up). The corrector
is a **no-go**: its premise died in a two-GPU-day probe instead of a
multi-day build. The incumbent's ~25× epoch-efficiency advantage
persists with local shortcuts now *excluded* as its mechanism on
strong bases; the round-2 probes below take up the remaining
suspects — and find that the boring one carries.

### The factorial, and the composition story

The members × trace factorial completed at the 16-GPU protocol
(anchors: plain 0.1019, trace 0.0503, members 0.0999;
@sec-nb-factorial-verdict):

| arm | final val | vs trace |
|---|---|---|
| members + trace | 0.0458 | 1.10× |
| **members + wide + trace** | **0.0270** | **1.86×** |

Members at reference width remains a near-null even post-trace
(+10%, echoing its +2% pre-trace). But trace and **width** compose
*super*-multiplicatively: trace bought 2.03× on the plain arm and
**3.7×** on the wide arm — width was starved *behind* the trace
defect. This is the interaction the flagship arm banks on.

### The flagship: composition confirmed

The all-mechanism composition — trace × members × wide ×
operator_layers 2, 1-node protocol — finished at
**0.0138/0.0140/0.0156** across its three seeds
(@sec-nb-flagship-verdict): every seed under the pre-registered
≤0.020 acceptance. Against the 3-seed depth rung (0.0224) the
composition buys another 1.60× — the mechanisms stack rather than
substitute, with the trace×width interaction carrying the load
exactly as the factorial predicted.

### H-C round 2: it's parameters, not rounds

With local shortcuts excluded, a structural diff of the incumbent's
source named the remaining suspects — per-point residual read-out,
learned soft-slice routing × 12 refinement rounds, LN-everywhere —
and one confound that round-1 discipline required excluding first:
**raw scale.** GeoTransolver runs ≈9.5M parameters; the flagship
≈0.6M — a 10–20× gap never tested (the early rank-doubling null was
rank-only, pre-trace, on the singpair base; the factorial had since
proven width×trace *super*-multiplicative). Two config-only ladders
on the flagship base answered both questions at once
(@sec-nb-hc2, @sec-nb-hc2-verdict):

| rung | params vs flagship | final val |
|---|---|---|
| flagship (×1) | 1× | 0.0140 (3-seed) |
| **scale: dims ×2** | ~4× | **0.0093 / 0.0095** (2 seeds) |
| scale: dims ×4 | ~16× | 0.0123 *at its stability LR/4 — see below* |
| iteration: 4 rounds, params matched | 1× | 0.0146 |
| iteration: 8 rounds, params matched | 1× | 0.0198 |
| iteration: 4 rounds, natural | ~2× | 0.0120 |
| iteration: 8 rounds, natural | ~4× | 0.0102 |

**The iterate-refine hypothesis is falsified at matched parameters**
— exchange-round count alone buys nothing (4 rounds flat, 8 rounds
actively worse), and natural-depth gains track their parameter
growth. **Scale carries**: ×2 dims meets its pre-registered ≥1.3×
bar with margin. Two honest flags. First, the ×4 rung froze at
initialization at the shared LR in both seeds (val 0.165 from ep1)
and trains only at LR/4 — a μP-style LR ∝ 1/width stability
constraint — where it finishes at **0.0123**, *worse* than ×2
despite 4× the parameters: **pure width bends under its own LR
constraint**, which is why the scale law below runs along the mixed
width×depth direction instead. Second, the incumbent's
epoch-efficiency edge *persists* (its ep-1 value still beats our ×2
arm's) — it just no longer implies a floor disadvantage. The rungs
PENDING at this round's close (further ×2 seeds, the
×2-dims-4-layer rung) landed and are the next section's subject.

### A provisional LR-stable frontier, and where parity sits on it

How far does "scale carries" carry? The pre-registered fit
(@sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict) answers on a fixed protocol: 1-node, 500
epochs, **LR-stable rungs only** — the ×4 point is excluded as
optimization-constrained (the width bend above). Seed calibration
first: the ×2 rung's four runs span 0.0090–0.0114 (±12% about the
mean), so single-seed rungs carry that error bar and the fit uses
per-rung means.

| rung | params | val (ep500) |
|---|---|---|
| flagship | 0.6M | 0.0140 (3-seed) |
| + operator_layers 4 (L4) | 1.2M | 0.0120 |
| + operator_layers 8 (L8) | 2.4M | 0.0102 |
| dims ×2 | 2.4M | 0.00979 (4-run mean) |
| dims ×2 + L4 (×2L4) | 4.8M | **0.00702** |
| dims ×2 + L8 (×2L8) | 9.6M | **0.005828** |

The fit over all six rungs:
$\text{val} \approx 0.0125 \cdot P_{\mathrm{M}}^{-0.33}$, rms
log-residual 0.052 — globally still a line, but with an honest
wrinkle at the top: the newest doubling's local slope flattened to
0.27 (×2→×2L4 was 0.42), a **mild bend at the 9.6M rung**
(@sec-nb-x2l8-verdict). Placing the incumbent's matched-protocol
anchor (0.00249 at ≈9.5M params) on that curve:

- At the incumbent's own budget the gap is now **measured, not
  extrapolated: 0.005828 at 9.6M — a 2.34× gap at matched
  parameters** (the curve had predicted 2.5×). The rung landed
  inside its pre-registered band (@sec-nb-scalelaw: 0.0050–0.0061;
  falsifier ≥ 0.0070 refuted), toward the band's shallow end —
  which is the bend above showing up exactly where the
  pre-registration said it would matter.
- **Parity by pure scaling recedes as the frontier bends**: the
  global slope projects ~134M parameters; if the newest local slope
  (0.27) persists, ~230M. Still mostly-single-seed, width and depth
  moving together, the LR-constrained ×4 point excluded — but the
  budget-matched rung is now a measurement, and it telegraphs the
  trend. **Program decision: the pure-scaling ladder stops at
  ×2L8.** The next factor of 2 is sought in per-parameter
  architectural efficiency (the separable far-field decode and
  kernel structure), not another rung; ×2L8 becomes the working
  scale reference.

The honest reading: scaling pays on a clean-but-bending frontier,
and the incumbent holds a **measured 2.34× per-parameter advantage
in-distribution**. The program's compensating assets are its
pre-registered bets — OOD generalization (next section, now under
the corrected vector metric), exact contracts, similarity
equivariance, zero-shot BC handling. Whether any of those is
*differential* rather than merely absolute was pre-registered as
the decisive comparison (@sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict), and the answer
turned out to be depth- and metric-dependent. **At zero-shot depth
the falsifier landed** (@sec-nb-geot-ood-zeroshot,
@sec-nb-corrected-zeroshot): under the corrected metric both
architectures degrade the same way (vector-WSS ~1.12× for each;
pressure ≤1.03 ours / ≤1.07 theirs) — no differential at the
boundary of the DoE hull, and the prediction that the incumbent
would degrade ≥1.5× was wrong. **At deep extremes a consistent
differential appeared** (@sec-nb-deep-differential): the OOD
section's paired exclusion-retrain comparison separates the
architectures on S1 with non-overlapping seed ranges — details
where the OOD evidence lives, below.

### The kernel factorial: the attribution verdict {#sec-drivaerml-factorial}

The external review's sharpest question was the one the industrial
program had skipped: is the exact boundary-integral structure — the
thesis mechanism — actually what carries the DrivAerML result? The
pre-registered test (@sec-nb-review,
@sec-nb-factorial-verdict-industrial): at the flagship rung, vary
ONLY the member dictionary, 1-node 500-epoch protocol, 3 seeds per
arm, against the flagship's own 3-seed control.

| arm | member dictionary | finals (3 seeds) | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| flagship (control) | 2 exact + 8 learned | 0.0138 / 0.0140 / 0.0156 | 0.0145 |
| exact-only | 2 exact (0 params) | 0.0144 / 0.0138 / 0.0156 | 0.0146 |
| MLP-only | 8 learned, no exact | 0.0153 / 0.0151 / 0.0167 | 0.0157 |

**The pre-registered falsifier fired.** The prediction was
MLP-only ≥ 1.25× the flagship; the measurement is 1.084×, with
overlapping seed bands. At this rung the in-distribution result is
carried by the rest of the architecture — the trace formulation,
typed attention and moments, and capacity — and the honest
description of the industrial model is **boundary-integral-inspired**.
Exact-kernel *causation* is established only where it was proven:
the synthetic program, whose ladders and margins stand unchanged.
The external review forced this test, and its skepticism was
substantially correct.

What survives is precise and worth having: exact-only beats
MLP-only on **every paired seed** (~7% each) — two closed-form,
zero-parameter members outperform eight learned ones at equal
non-member parameters — and exact-only is indistinguishable from
the flagship itself (0.0146 vs 0.0145), which makes the flagship's
eight learned members **evidence-orphaned at this rung**: the
simpler exact-only configuration is a parsimony candidate for the
default. The thesis's second barrel then fired the same way: the
**zero-shot OOD rider** (all six factorial checkpoints on the
never-seen S1/S2 splits, corrected vector metric,
@sec-nb-rider-verdict) measured *indistinguishable* degradation
ratios — MLP-only 1.11–1.14×, exact-only 1.11–1.13× — refuting the
prediction that exact far-field structure would matter more
off-distribution. **The exact-kernel demotion at this rung is
total**: neither in-distribution accuracy nor OOD robustness. The
exact dictionary's ~7% absolute edge does carry into OOD errors
(an accuracy offset, not a robustness slope), and one exploratory
counterpoint is on record: at the 9.6M ×2L8 rung, removing the
learned members costs ~9% (0.00635 vs 0.00583) — single seed
against a known ±12% rung spread, so the default configuration
keeps its members and the parsimony swap is not adopted.

### The trace factorial: the dominant mechanism, decomposed {#sec-drivaerml-trace-factorial}

If the exact kernels do not carry the industrial result, what does?
The trace factorial answers with the program's cleanest attribution
(@sec-nb-trace-factorial-verdict; pre-registered as review item 3's
decomposition, with the no-trace control added mid-campaign when
the kernel factorial demonstrated that effect sizes measured at
small configurations need not survive scale). Same protocol
discipline as every arm above: 1-node, 500 epochs, 3 seeds,
flagship capacity, one mechanism toggled at a time.

| arm | jump correction | trace readouts | finals (3 seeds) | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no-trace | – | – | 0.0525 / 0.0524 / 0.0604 | 0.0551 |
| correction-only | ✓ | – | 0.0148 / 0.0153 / 0.0161 | 0.0154 |
| readouts-only | – | ✓ | 0.0149 / 0.0151 / 0.0162 | 0.0154 |
| flagship (both) | ✓ | ✓ | 0.0138 / 0.0140 / 0.0156 | 0.0145 |

Two findings, both structural:

1. **Trace is the dominant mechanism of the industrial program:
   3.8× at flagship capacity.** It *grew* from the 2.03× measured at
   the small pre-ladder configuration — the mirror image of the
   kernel members, whose effect compressed to noise at the same
   rung. Mechanisms scale individually; measuring each at the
   operating configuration is the only honest attribution. The
   ranking at flagship now reads: trace 3.8× ≫ capacity (the
   frontier's 2.4× from 0.6M→9.6M) ≫ member dictionary (0–8%).
2. **The two trace sub-mechanisms are near-perfect substitutes.**
   Correction-only and readouts-only land within 0.1% of each other,
   each recovering ~96% of the log-gap; enabling both adds a final
   ~6%. The mechanistic reading: the load-bearing information is
   *boundary self-identification* — a channel telling the decoder
   that a query point IS the boundary at its own panel. The exact
   exterior jump constant (+½, zero parameters, licensed by the
   jump relation) and the learned own-cell readouts each deliver
   that bit; once either does, the other is largely redundant. The
   default keeps both (the 6% is free at inference); any future
   variant — including the separable far-field decode — must
   preserve at least one such channel, and the exact correction is
   the principled zero-parameter choice.

### Generalization: the OOD protocol and its verdict

This is the program's north-star axis — a surrogate that only
interpolates its training geometry is not an engineering tool — and
DrivAerML shipped with no out-of-distribution evaluation at all. We
defined one, in the dataset's own generative coordinates: the
upstream design-of-experiments varies 16 shape parameters, and 483
of the 484 runs carry their official DoE values
(@sec-nb-ood-protocol). Two splits were adopted, each with a
leakage audit:

- **S2 — wake-topology corner** (primary): the joint top decile of
  backlight angle + rear-end tapering, **49 held-out cars** — the
  two-factor extreme that flips rear-wake topology. Median margin
  along the score direction ≈ 37× the training-set spacing.
- **S1 — ride-height double-extreme**: top and bottom deciles of
  ride height, **98 cars** — single-factor extrapolation in both
  directions on ground-effect physics.
- A third candidate (a neighborhood carve) was honestly downgraded:
  a space-filling 16-D DoE leaves no interior holes (nearest-
  neighbor ratio 0.98×), so it tests nothing.

**Boundary read (zero-shot).** The standard-split flagship, evaluated
on the OOD cars it never saw — with the overlap stated plainly: the
standard 435-car training set already contains 88/98 of S1 and 45/49
of S2, so the valid zero-shot sets are the never-seen remainder
(**n = 10 and 4**, at the *boundary* margin of the OOD regions),
against 36 never-seen in-distribution cars as the matched reference.
Degradation under the corrected vector metric
(@sec-nb-corrected-zeroshot, superseding the direction-blind
aggregate of @sec-nb-ood-zeroshot): **pressure 1.00–1.03×, but
vector WSS 1.12–1.13×** across three seeds — the WSS penalty is
real and resolvable above seed spread. The old metric compared
magnitudes only and had hidden the hardest part of the field:
for both this model and the incumbent, **WSS direction error is
~3× the magnitude error** (ours 0.72 vs 0.21 relative L2 at the ID
reference; the incumbent's 0.28 vs 0.09), and the incumbent's
zero-shot WSS ratios sit in the same band (1.12–1.16×).

**Deep read (OOD-trained).** The decisive version: retrain the
flagship on the OOD-train sets (385/434 cars; validation from a
carve of the same distribution, extremes untouched by selection),
then evaluate each run on its **full** held-out extreme set — 98/98
and 49/49 cars, three seeds per protocol, each run against its own
in-distribution reference so the smaller-training-set effect cancels
(@sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict):

All WSS figures below use the corrected joint-component vector
metric (@sec-nb-deep-differential; the direction-blind magnitude
figures of the original table survive in the notebook as
`wss_mag`). Ratios are each run's extremes against its own ID
reference:

| protocol | seed | ID ref (p / wss rel-L2) | extremes (p / wss) | degradation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 (n=98) | 42 | 0.195 / 0.779 | 0.198 / 0.845 | 1.02× / 1.09× |
| S1 | 43 | 0.176 / 0.721 | 0.181 / 0.783 | 1.03× / 1.09× |
| S1 | 44 | 0.226 / 0.919 | 0.233 / 0.985 | 1.03× / 1.07× |
| S2 (n=49) | 42 | 0.187 / 0.815 | 0.192 / 0.787 | 1.03× / 0.97× |
| S2 | 43 | 0.175 / 0.772 | 0.180 / 0.755 | 1.03× / 0.98× |
| S2 | 44 | 0.184 / 0.797 | 0.189 / 0.776 | 1.03× / 0.97× |

The pre-registered bars were ≤2× (S1) and ≤3× (S2); the measured
degradation is **pressure 1.02–1.03× everywhere, vector WSS
1.07–1.09× on S1 and none on S2** (slightly inverted — the
wake-topology corner does not stress WSS direction at all). The
excess degradation remains 11–100× smaller than the allowed excess.
Integrated drag concurs: 4.5–5.4% relative CD error in-distribution
vs 6–7% on the S1 extremes, 4–6% on both for S2.

**The differential — sealed at five seeds on WSS; pressure demoted.**
The incumbent's exclusion-retrain arms — same splits, harness,
metric, and protocol — give the paired comparison the zero-shot
read could not, now at five seeds per model
(@sec-nb-deep-differential, sealed in @sec-nb-seal-verdict):

| model | S1 press ratio | S1 wss ratio | S2 press | S2 wss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this program (5 seeds) | 1.019–1.044 | **1.072–1.113** | 1.03 | 0.97–0.98 |
| incumbent (5 seeds) | 1.043–1.069 | **1.126–1.136** | 1.03–1.05 | 0.99 |

On S1 vector WSS the seed ranges are disjoint at 5-vs-5 (exact
rank-sum p ≈ 0.008): the incumbent's mean excess degradation is
1.4× ours (0.131 vs 0.092). The pre-registered extension sharpened
the estimate honestly in both directions — the effect survived its
falsifier (no overlap), but the original "ours ≤ 1.10" bound broke
(seeds 45/46 came in at 1.113/1.104), so the sealed effect is
thinner than the 3-seed read suggested (1.4×, not 1.65×). On
pressure the extension ranges TOUCH (our 1.044 vs their 1.043):
per the same falsifier logic the pressure differential is demoted
to *suggestive* — consistent ordering of means (1.031 vs 1.056),
not seed-separated. Scope stated plainly: the differential is in
generalization *ratios* — absolute errors still favor the incumbent
~2.5–2.7× everywhere (its capacity advantage), and both models sit
far inside the engineering bars.

*How to read this — and how not to.* Both caveats inline: the drag
figures are **pseudo-coefficients** (predicted and true fields
integrated on the same 10k-cell subsample — a valid error measure,
not comparable to full-mesh CD values); and the extremes are
**parameter-space extrapolation within the DrivAer family** — real
aerodynamic regime shifts (wake topology, ground effect), but not
novel vehicle topologies. Within that stated scope: **geometry
generalization on the industrial benchmark holds at ~3% (pressure)
and ~8% (vector WSS, S1 only) degradation — boundary and deep, both
protocols, three seeds each — and, at deep-S1, measurably better
than the incumbent's on both fields, pending the 5-seed seal.**

### Decode efficiency: the 14× repricing

The profile that the cluster's idle-GPU telemetry forced
(@sec-nb-decode-profile) found a 102k-launch dispatch storm in the
shared closed-forms path (an `einsum` lowering to a 4.2×10⁷-batch
bmm) and a deliberately-sequential bitwise member loop. Both fixed —
the second under a physics-lined contract split
(@sec-nb-contract-split): closed forms stay bitwise, learned members
move to measured-tolerance GEMMs with a bitwise reference mode
retained. Result: **7.2× (singpair) and 14.2× (members) step
speedups**, 474/474 tests, live on both clusters. Every wall-clock
number in this chapter is now ~an order of magnitude cheaper than
when it was measured.

The last decode economy is configuration, not code. The
checkpointed query-chunk decode — mandatory at B200 memory — costs
~10× on the 278-GB B300s, where the whole batched decode fits. The
paired same-seed control (@sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict) licenses
turning it off: ×2 rung, seed 42, chunked 0.0093 vs unchunked
0.00896 — **accuracy-neutral** (the 3.7% is inside the rung's seed
noise), so unchunked is the default for every rung from here. The
earlier unchunked outlier that raised the question (0.0114, seed
44) was seed variance, and is counted in the ±12% spread the scale
law's error bars carry.
